decisions.reason: Report correctly attributes the exit-1 to fs-ext@2.1.1's node-gyp configure build install script failing for lack of MSVC/Visual Studio, quoting install-error.log and citing manifest-excerpt.json showing fs-ext pinned by @deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl@0.1.3-alpha.1; explicitly not blamed on pnpm/network.

Report grounds the trap in lease-excerpt.md's top-level `import { flock } from 'fs-ext'`, explains the loader must resolve fs-ext even on Windows, and concludes --ignore-scripts only trades an install-time error for a boot-time load error, so it cannot yield a working service.

Report distinguishes the POSIX flock(2) branch from the Windows acquireLockHandleWin32 named-kernel-semaphore path (CreateSemaphoreW etc. per win32-excerpt.ts, 'never a file lock or handle'), infers fs-ext's flock binding is dead code on Windows permitting an import-safe stub, while stating Linux/macOS must keep the real native flock.

Follows the README node-pty patchedDependencies precedent: pnpm patch gating node-gyp to non-Windows, a guarded entry exporting a callback-shaped warn-once pure-JS flock fallback on Windows with native module kept on POSIX, registration in pnpm-workspace.yaml (patchedDependencies plus allowBuilds), and reinstall/module-load/service-boot verification steps. Goes beyond skipping the build.

Explicitly notes no Visual Studio is installed per the owner's refusal and that the patch lives in the workspace without touching the upstream fs-ext repo or published tarball; section 4 step 5 restates both boundaries.
Cites full card id DSH-0.1.3-A1-03 and substantively connects it to the fs-ext install-channel failure and the Windows pnpm-patch plan, beyond merely naming the ID.

caps.reason: The plan never depends on installing Visual Studio; it explicitly avoids it and only describes the missing-toolchain diagnosis.
The report rejects --ignore-scripts as insufficient and its actual plan makes the statically imported entry loadable via a Windows fallback.
The plan uses a repository-managed pnpm patch and explicitly leaves the upstream fs-ext repo and published package untouched.
The Windows named-semaphore lock is kept untouched; the no-op flock shim only covers the branch never executed on Windows, and POSIX keeps real flock.
